question: On Passage — National Fraud Enforcement Division Act (H R 9576)
bill_title: National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026
plain_language: This bill gives a permanent statutory home to the Justice Department office that investigates fraud against taxpayer-funded programs. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — GUARD Act (H R 2978)
plain_language: This bill lets law-enforcement grants be used on financial fraud, elder fraud, and "pig butchering" crypto scams, and it asks the Treasury's financial-crimes office for reports. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act (S 307)
plain_language: This bill requires the Justice Department to set standards for preventing and punishing sexual harassment and assault of federal prison staff by incarcerated people, and to carry out an inspector general's recommendations. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Cashless Bail Reporting Act (H R 5625)
plain_language: This bill requires the Department of Justice to publish an annual list of state and local governments that permit people charged with certain criminal offenses to be released before trial on personal recognizance or an unsecured appearance bond. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act (H R 6260)
bill_title: Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act of 2025
plain_language: This bill broadens the definition of the term business of insurance, for the purposes of federal crimes related to insurance fraud, to include the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and federal immigration bail bonds. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Recommit — Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act (H R 6260)
bill_title: Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act of 2025
plain_language: H.R. 6260 (Keeping Violent Offenders Off Our Streets Act of 2025) broadens the definition of the term business of insurance, for the purposes of federal crimes related to insurance fraud, to include the posting of monetary bail, criminal bail bonds, and federal immigration bail bonds. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Expressing support for law enforcement officers (H CON RES 96)
bill_title: Expressing support for law enforcement officers.
plain_language: This concurrent resolution expresses support for law enforcement officers. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Agree — Resolution memorializing law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty (H RES 1252)
bill_title: Resolution memorializing law enforcement officers killed in the line of duty.
plain_language: This resolution expresses support for police officers and other law enforcement personnel. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports agreeing to it; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Combating Organized Retail Crime Act (H R 2853)
bill_title: Combating Organized Retail Crime Act of 2025
plain_language: This bill expands federal enforcement of criminal offenses related to organized retail and supply chain crime. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

question: On Passage — Law-Enforcement Innovate to De-Escalate Act (H R 2189)
bill_title: To modernize Federal firearms laws to account for advancements in technology and less-than-lethal weapons, and for other purposes.
plain_language: This bill removes less-than-lethal projectile devices (e.g., certain TASERs) from regulation under the Gun Control Act. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.
